newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich yr pretax up 18 pct before float.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich yr pretax up 18 pct before float.

text.p: Britain's Woolwich Building Society, one of a number of these mutually-owned financial institutions planning to float this year, said on Wednesday that its pretax profit rose by 18 percent to 392 million pounds ($629.5 million) in 1996, excluding conversion costs.

While its net mortgage lending jumped by 50 percent to 1.4 billion pounds, the society said its administrative expenses rose by less than one percent and its cost-to-income ratio edged down to 45.8 percent from 48.9 percent.

"This represents another strong performance by the Woolwich with the achievement of record profits and improvements in key operating ratios. We are well placed for further growth in the UK, France and Italy following conversion and flotation in July," chief executive John Stewart said in the statement.
The society said that 1996 ended up being "its most profitable year ever", with improvements in all key operating rations which measure its performance relative to overheads.

After July's conversion, the Woolwich expects to become a company listed in the London Stock Exchange's FTSE 100 list of top companies. It has a customer base of over four million investors and borrowers, many of whom are set to become shareholders as it distributes its capital on conversion.
It made a 15.4 million pound charge for conversion costs to its profit and loss account. ($1=.6227 Pound)
